content.text:
Done. The fix is one line in `lib/request.js:262`.

## What was wrong

`port` read `this.headers.host ?? this.headers[':authority']` directly, while `host` (plain builder) reads `this.raw.headers.host ?? this.raw.headers[':authority']` and the trust-proxy builder overrides `host` to prefer `x-forwarded-host`. With `trustProxy` on, `host`/`hostname` came from the forwarded header but `port` came from the real `Host` header — the three disagreed.

## Change

`lib/request.js` — `port` now parses `this.host`. Parsing logic from #6603 is unchanged (same regex, same `null` when absent, same IPv6 handling). Because `port` lives on `Request.prototype` and `host` is overridden on the trust-proxy prototype that inherits from it, the getter resolves to the effective host in both builders — so the plain and trust-proxy variants stay in step without duplicating the getter, and `:authority` fallback is inherited from `host` rather than re-implemented.

## Tests

- `test/request-port.test.js` — added trust-proxy coverage: `x-forwarded-host` winning over `host`, forwarded host *without* a port yielding `null` even when `Host` has one, last entry of a multi-value forwarded host, IPv6 forwarded host, fallback to `host`, fallback to `:authority`, no host info at all, plus an untrusted-connection case. Each fixture also asserts `host`/`hostname`/`port` agree.
- `test/trust-proxy.test.js` — the existing shared `testRequestValues` asserted `req.port === app.server.address().port` while sending `X-Forwarded-Host: fastify.test` (no port). That encoded the old, misaligned behavior, so those expectations are now `null` (the forwarded host carries no port), the helper checks `'port' in options` with a single assertion, and `t.plan` counts were adjusted. Added two end-to-end tests to keep positive coverage: a trusted `X-Forwarded-Host: fastify.test:8080` yielding port `8080`, and an untrusted connection falling back to the real `Host` header's port.

`docs/Reference/Request.md` already documents `port` as "The port parsed from `request.host`", so it needed no change.

## Co-change partner

`lib/reply.js` (40% co-change with `lib/request.js`) needed **no** change — its only `host` reference is the `INVALID_TRAILERS` blocklist at `lib/reply.js:299`; it derives nothing from host or port.

Verified: `test/request-port.test.js`, `test/trust-proxy.test.js`, `test/internals/request.test.js`, `test/internals/reply.test.js`, `test/request-header-host.test.js`, `test/request-media-type.test.js`, `test/hostname.test.js`, `test/http2/*`, plus every other suite referencing `req.port` (`url-rewriting`, `https`, `async-await`, `http-methods/get`, `server`) — all pass. I could not run `eslint` (the command needed approval I don't have), so the new test code is style-matched by hand rather than lint-verified. Nothing committed.

All 8 diagnostics-channel suites pass (8/8), on top of the request/reply/trust-proxy suites I ran earlier.

**Co-change partner `lib/reply.js`: no change needed.** Its only host-related reference is the `INVALID_TRAILERS` blocklist entry at `lib/reply.js:299`; it derives nothing from `host`, `hostname`, or `port`, and the change is confined to a getter on the request prototype, so the response path is unaffected.

Final state of the work:

- `lib/request.js:262` — `port` now parses `this.host` instead of reading `headers.host` / `headers[':authority']` directly, so `host`, `hostname`, and `port` share one effective-host source. Parsing logic from #6603 unchanged. The trust-proxy builder needs no separate `port` getter: it overrides `host` on a prototype inheriting from `Request.prototype`, so the plain and trust-proxy variants stay in step by construction.
- `test/request-port.test.js` — added trust-proxy fixtures (forwarded host winning over `Host`, forwarded host without a port yielding `null`, multi-value forwarded host, IPv6, `host` fallback, `:authority` fallback, no host info, untrusted connection), each also asserting the three properties agree.
- `test/trust-proxy.test.js` — updated the stale expectations that encoded the old misalignment, and added two end-to-end tests (trusted `X-Forwarded-Host: fastify.test:8080` → `8080`; untrusted → real `Host` port).

`docs/Reference/Request.md` already describes `port` as parsed from `request.host`, so it needed no edit. `eslint` could not be run (the command required approval), so the new test code is style-matched by hand rather than lint-verified. Nothing committed.
